problem: Consider the equation $\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{6})+3=0$ for $-\pi <x\le \pi .$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{4}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Containing a Transformed Tangent Function Under a Modified Domain
examples.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+\frac{\pi }{4} & =\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =-\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi  \\ 3x & =n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{n\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0, \pm 1, \pm 2,\ldots,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $-\pi < x \leq \pi.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=0.$

- Setting $n=\pm1$ gives $x=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{3}.$

- Setting $n=\pm2$ gives $x=\pm\dfrac{2\pi}{3}.$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\pi.$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $-\pi < x \leq \pi.$ So, the solutions are

$$
x = 0,\, \pm \dfrac{\pi}{3},\, \pm\dfrac{2\pi}{3}, \, \pi.
$$

feedback.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{3})=-\sqrt{3}$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ Given that the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-\frac{\pi }{3} & =-\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{n\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=0$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\pi $

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\frac{3\pi }{2}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=0,\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ,\frac{3\pi }{2}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{2}=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and ${x}_{3}=\pi ,$ we have

$$
{x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot \pi =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2}.
$$
